userStories.title: Record the fix-commit SHA on every finish round
acceptanceCriteria: When a `commit_<phase>` node runs with a dirty working tree, then its appended audit round has `sha` equal to the `HEAD` SHA reported by `git rev-parse HEAD` after the commit.
When a `commit_<phase>` node runs with a clean working tree, then its appended audit round has `committed: false` and no `sha` field.
When an audit-trail JSONL line contains `sha`, then `readRounds` returns the round with that `sha` preserved.
When `writeResult` writes a result after recorded rounds contain `sha`, then its `rounds[]` entries carry each recorded SHA.

routing.reasoning: A small cross-file data-contract extension using established flow and JSONL seams.

userStories.title: Build deterministic finish PR title and body
acceptanceCriteria: When `buildFinishTitle` receives a context with feature `<feature>`, then it returns `feat: <feature>`.
When `buildFinishBody` receives stories, then it renders one `| <id> | <title> | <acCount> |` row per story.
When a story title contains `|`, then `buildFinishBody` escapes it so its table row remains three columns.
When `acceptance` is present, then `buildFinishBody` renders its Verification line.
When `regression` is present, then `buildFinishBody` renders its Verification line.
When `gatesRan` contains gate names, then `buildFinishBody` renders a Verification line listing every name.
When `diffstat` is present, then `buildFinishBody` includes its text verbatim in Verification.
When rounds are present, then `buildFinishBody` renders one heading naming each round's `phase` and `attempt`.
When a round has findings, then `buildFinishBody` renders each finding as a bullet carrying its `severity` and `title`.
When a committed round has `sha`, then `buildFinishBody` renders its abbreviated seven-character SHA in that round heading.
When a round has `committed: false`, then `buildFinishBody` renders no SHA in that round heading.
When `rounds` is empty, then `buildFinishBody` returns no `Review rounds` heading.
When `outOfScope` has entries, then `buildFinishBody` renders one unchanged-text bullet per entry.
When `outOfScope` is empty, then `buildFinishBody` returns no `Out of scope` heading.
When run counts and duration are present, then `buildFinishBody` renders one footer line as `<storiesPassed>/<storiesTotal> stories · <durationMs formatted as Nm SSs>`.

routing.reasoning: A new pure formatter with precise markdown behavior and an existing builder to mirror.

userStories.title: Load PRD and status artifacts into the PR context
acceptanceCriteria: When the PRD has `userStories[]`, then `loadFinishPrContext` returns one story per entry with its `id`, `title`, and `acceptanceCriteria` length as `acCount`.
When the PRD has `outOfScope`, then `loadFinishPrContext` returns the same array as `outOfScope`.
When called with `FinishInput.feature`, then `loadFinishPrContext` returns that value as `feature`.
When loading status, then `loadFinishPrContext` reads `status.json` in the same directory as `input.prdPath`.
When `input.prdPath` is relative, then `loadFinishPrContext` resolves its sibling status path against `input.workdir`.
When status has `postRun.acceptance.status`, then `loadFinishPrContext` returns it as `acceptance`.
When status has `postRun.regression.status`, then `loadFinishPrContext` returns it as `regression`.
When status has `durationMs`, then `loadFinishPrContext` returns it as `run.durationMs`.
When status has `progress.passed`, then `loadFinishPrContext` returns it as `run.storiesPassed`.
When status has `progress.total`, then `loadFinishPrContext` returns it as `run.storiesTotal`.
When the PRD file does not exist, then `loadFinishPrContext` does not throw and returns empty `stories` and `outOfScope`.
When the PRD file is invalid JSON, then `loadFinishPrContext` does not throw and returns empty `stories` and `outOfScope`.
When the status file does not exist, then `loadFinishPrContext` does not throw and returns `acceptance` and `regression` as undefined.
When the status file is invalid JSON, then `loadFinishPrContext` does not throw and returns `acceptance` and `regression` as undefined.

routing.reasoning: Extends the new loader with clear file shapes and fail-open parsing paths.

userStories.title: Load rounds, diffstat, and gate names into the PR context
acceptanceCriteria: When `readRounds` returns rounds for the input, then `loadFinishPrContext` returns those rounds with each `sha` preserved.
When called with `args.gatesRan`, then `loadFinishPrContext` returns that array as `gatesRan`.
When called with a base branch, then `loadFinishPrContext` invokes `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD` using that base.
When the diffstat command succeeds, then `loadFinishPrContext` returns its stdout as `diffstat`.
When the diffstat command exits non-zero, then `loadFinishPrContext` does not throw and returns `diffstat` as undefined.
When the run audit-trail file does not exist, then `loadFinishPrContext` does not throw and returns an empty `rounds` array.

routing.reasoning: Completes a loader across existing audit, git, and flow-output seams with a constrained type widening.

userStories.title: Write finished title and body on every forge path
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Use the deterministic finish metadata when opening, promoting, or retaining a ready PR/MR, while preserving a fail-open PR creation path.

**Motivation** — `openOrPromotePr` only runs `gh pr ready` for auto-PR drafts and never rewrites title or body, so it keeps a body composed before the run finished.

**Approach** — `openOrPromotePr` keeps its `(repoRoot, branch, title, body)` signature and its `{ status, url }` return; the `promoted` and `already-ready` paths gain a title/body write. `open_pr` loads context with `loadCtxOf(ctx).base` and `gateOutputs(ctx).ran`, builds title/body, and passes them to `openOrPromotePr`. `gh pr edit` / `glab mr update` non-zero exits are non-fatal and preserve the returned promoted/already-ready status and URL. If context loading or a builder throws, fall back to `nax-finish: <feature>` and `Automated finish of `<feature>`.` and still open the PR. The `nothing-to-finish` early return remains before context loading.

**Scope** — In: every normal forge path's metadata write, flow wiring, and fallback. Out: the escalation draft PR retains its existing title/body; do not alter auto-PR plugin behavior or templates.

**Interface**
```typescript
export async function openOrPromotePr(
  repoRoot: string,
  branch: string,
  title: string,
  body: string,
): Promise<{ status: "opened" | "promoted" | "already-ready"; url?: string }>;
```
acceptanceCriteria: When a GitHub branch has a draft PR, then `openOrPromotePr` invokes `gh pr edit <branch> --title <title> --body <body>` after `gh pr ready`.
When a GitHub branch has a draft PR, then `openOrPromotePr` returns status `promoted`.
When a GitHub branch has a non-draft PR, then `openOrPromotePr` invokes `gh pr edit <branch> --title <title> --body <body>` and returns status `already-ready`.
When a GitHub branch has no PR, then `openOrPromotePr` invokes `gh pr create` with its received `--title` and `--body` values and returns status `opened`.
When a GitLab branch has a draft MR, then `openOrPromotePr` invokes `glab mr update <branch> --title <title> --description <body>`.
When `gh pr edit` exits non-zero after promotion, then `openOrPromotePr` does not throw and returns status `promoted` with the PR URL.
When `glab mr update` exits non-zero while writing finish metadata, then `openOrPromotePr` does not throw and returns its promoted or already-ready status with the MR URL.
When `buildFinishTitle` is stubbed to return a known string and the flow `open_pr` node runs, then it passes that string as the title to `openOrPromotePr`.
When `buildFinishBody` is stubbed to return a known string and the flow `open_pr` node runs, then it passes that string as the body to `openOrPromotePr`.
When the flow `open_pr` node sees `load_ctx.route` equal to `nothing-to-finish`, then it returns without invoking `loadFinishPrContext`.
When `loadFinishPrContext` throws in the flow `open_pr` node, then it still invokes `openOrPromotePr` with fallback title `nax-finish: <feature>`.

When `buildFinishTitle` or `buildFinishBody` throws in the flow `open_pr` node, then it still invokes `openOrPromotePr` with fallback title `nax-finish: <feature>` and fallback body `Automated finish of `<feature>`.`.

routing.reasoning: Cross-module flow wiring and multiple external forge state paths require isolated test, implementation, and verification passes.

analysis: This is an enhancement to the acpx-hosted `flows/nax-finish` module, not to the Bun `src/` tree. `flows/nax-finish/nax-finish.flow.ts:223-252` calls `commitFixes`, appends the live audit record, and currently discards `shaAfter`; `FinishRound` at `flows/nax-finish/types.ts:45-56` therefore cannot preserve a fix SHA, although `steps/result.ts:76-107` JSONL-serializes, reads, and embeds whole rounds in the terminal result. `flows/nax-finish/nax-finish.flow.ts:433-447` is the sole normal open_pr integration point: after `commitAndPush`, it supplies the placeholder title/body to `openOrPromotePr`. `openOrPromotePr` in `flows/nax-finish/steps/pr.ts:31-71` already has the stable four-argument contract and handles create, draft promotion, and already-ready paths, but only create receives body metadata today. Its injectable `_prDeps.run` and `test/unit/flows/nax-finish/steps/pr.test.ts` command-capture pattern are the right seams for fail-open edit tests. `flows/nax-finish/flow-ctx.ts:52-56` hides `quality_gates.ran` behind a return type exposing only `failing`; the accessor must widen without breaking existing callers. The green `quality_gates` route emits `ran` at `flows/nax-finish/nax-finish.flow.ts:403-405`, so no new gate data needs to be persisted. The new flow-local `steps/pr-body.ts` must use Node APIs and `_prBodyDeps` because flow modules execute under Node/acpx; `steps/quality.ts:10-30` demonstrates ENOENT-as-absent reads and `scripts/check-flows-no-bun.ts` statically prohibits Bun in flows. It must deliberately mirror, not import, the pure auto-PR builder in `src/plugins/builtin/auto-pr/pr-body.ts:38-107`: `buildTitle` establishes `feat: <feature>`, while `escapeTableCell` escapes backslashes, pipes, and newlines. Loader inputs are existing PRD/status artifacts plus `readRounds`, `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD`, and gate output; relative `prdPath` requires resolution from `FinishInput.workdir`. Main risks are accidentally violating the src→flows runtime boundary, blocking PR creation on optional artifact/forge-edit failures, malformed markdown from table cells, and pushing the 568-line flow over its 600-line hard cap. Keep formatting and I/O in the new module, make every artifact read and diff fail-open, use fallback literals only when builder loading/building throws, and preserve the current create/promotion error behavior except for non-fatal metadata edits. No data migration is required: `sha` is optional, old audit lines remain readable, and status/PRD schemas are read-only inputs. Existing focused coverage lives in `test/unit/flows/nax-finish/flow-commits.test.ts`, `steps/result.test.ts`, and `steps/pr.test.ts`; add a dedicated `steps/pr-body.test.ts` and extend the established flow-node harness for wiring/fallback behavior.
outOfScope: A model-written "What changed" narrative section is not part of this spec; the body is assembled deterministically from artifacts, with no agent call in the `open_pr` path.
Lifting the spec's `## Summary` heading into the PR body as a narrative substitute is not part of this spec.
Honouring the repository's `.github/pull_request_template.md` in the finish-opened PR is not part of this spec; `findPrTemplate` in `src/plugins/builtin/auto-pr/template.ts` stays auto-PR-only.

Sharing code with `src/plugins/builtin/auto-pr/pr-body.ts` is not part of this spec; `src/` and `flows/` are separate modules loaded by different runtimes, and the finish builder is a flow-local reimplementation.
Changing the auto-PR plugin's own title, body or template behaviour is not part of this spec.

The escalation draft PR opened by `flows/nax-finish/steps/escalate.ts:71` keeps its existing `nax-finish: <branch>` title and escalation-comment body; only the `open_pr` node's PR is retitled and rewritten.
Adding new fields to `status.json` or `prd.json` is not part of this spec; the builder reads only fields that already exist.
The run's accumulated cost (`cost.spent` in `status.json`) is deliberately not reported anywhere in the PR body; the footer reports story counts and duration only.
Reconciling the `nax-finish` result schema with any downstream consumer other than the PR body is not part of this spec.
